To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have completed the classification of scattered polynomials, which are exceptional in the sense defined in the abstract, for the index $0$ case when the characteristic $q$ is less than or equal to 4.
the classification of exceptional scattered linear sets is completed for $q=2$, and that the classification of scattered polynomials is completed for $t=0,2$, and $q \le 5$.
we have completed the classification of exceptional scattered polynomial of index 0 for $q \in \{3,4\}$ and of index 2 for $q \geq 3$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the full classification of scattered polynomials for $q=2$, $q=3$ and $q=4$.
the classification of exceptional scattered linear sets in ${\rm AG}(2,q^{mr})$.
the full classification of scattered monic polinomials of index $0$, $1$ and $2$. [1]
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for any $t$ and $q$ there are only finitely many exceptional scattered monic polynomial of index $2$, except for the case $(t,q)=(0,3)$.

the classification of exceptional scattered polynomial is complete for $q \geq 5$ and $t \leq 2$; it is complete for $t \le 1$, for $q \in \{2,3\}$; it is partial for $q \equiv 1$ mod $4$ and for $q \ne 2$, and it is open in all other cases.
the classification of scattered polynomials is almost complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we classify the exceptional scattered monic linear polynomials of index 0, 1 and 2.
, for $t=0,1,2$, all exceptional scattered monic polynomial of index $i$ have been classified.
we have classified all exceptional scattered polynomials with $t \leq 3$ for $q\leq 4$ and for $t \le 2$ for arbitrary $q$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complete classification of the exceptional scattered polynomials is within reach.
there are no exceptional scattered polynomials for $q>4$, except for index $1$.
the complete classification of all exceptional scattered monic $q$-polyomials of index $t$, for $t \geq 2$, is a very challenging problem.
